rationale: The Court is most likely to reverse unanimously on the narrow Mitchell/Jicarilla ground that no specific statute, treaty, or regulation creates an enforceable affirmative duty to quantify needs and secure Lower Colorado River Mainstream water, with decree/finality concerns as reinforcing context. Roberts is best positioned to assign and write a minimalist opinion, though Thomas is a strong alternative author given the conference’s emphasis on his textual trust-duty framework and the likelihood of one or more concurrences (especially from Gorsuch/Alito/Thomas) elaborating on decree-retained-jurisdiction or separation-of-powers limits.
